messages.author: 567c323bbfbe3754
messages.subject: Data security
parts:
Hello,  

I'm working with the free version of shinyapps.io.  

My program asks users to upload data from their computer for processing.  

Is this a secure process?  Can the user be sure that the uploaded data is not available to others?

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Data security
parts:
Hi Charles,
The transfer is secure since it is over SSL.   Whatever you write to the disk (if you do write anything) will be transient so you should be okay on that front.

Best,
Tareef

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Data security
parts:
Selva, Charles,
Thank you for your questions and concerns.  Shinyapps.io was built to allow for the isolation of different people's application and data from each other.  As part of our paid tiers, you will be able to restrict access to who can see/use your application through the authentication mechanism we provide.  In the coming two weeks we will be introducing a new way to do authentication which would allow you to require people to authenticate through their Google Authentication, GitHub authentication or using password based authentication in our service.   None of these address the question of how you are storing your data within the application and how you go about reading/writing your data which would need to be managed by you in your application.  All access to the service is over SSL which is a best practice for eliminating a class of security exploits.  

To answer Charles's request.  The entire infrastructure is hosted in a SAS70 compliant facility, any credit card information we gather will be managed by a 3rd party provider who is PCI compliant as we will not be storing any financial instruments in our system to avoid needing to meet the PCI requirements.  A few of the security standards you refer to Charles are only relevant for financial data hosting which we aren't really targeting for shinyapps.io  In the interest of full transparency we have also put together some docs which capture our various policies and how we would use data that we could collect.

This service is new and we know that there are certain use cases that may not be a good fit for a hosted offering.  if your organization doesn't typically allow data to leave their firewalls, then shinyapps.io is unlikely to be the right fit for you and it might be better for you to consider an on-premise version of Shiny Server to host your applications on.

I hope this helps clarify the issue.  Feel free to send along any other questions you have.

-Tareef
